name: Tao Wen
position: Research Fellow in AI Trust and Security
bio: I am a Research Fellow in AI Trust and Security at Alliance Manchester Business School, The University of Manchester, where I work with Professor Richard Allmendinger. I am also an Academic Fellow at Ofcom (Office of Communications).

My research focuses on understanding how information, beliefs, and behaviours co-evolve within complex interconnected systems, and how these dynamics affect collective outcomes and decision-making. I combine network science, computational modelling, agent-based approaches, and decision analytics to study misinformation diffusion, opinion dynamics, game theory, and trustworthy AI, with particular interests in the co-evolution of information, social structure and individual behaviour. I also investigate Parrondo’s paradox, strategy switching, and emergent collective behaviour in complex systems. Beyond social systems, I extend these computational approaches to transport and maritime networks, exploring their resilience and coordination and supporting transitions towards more sustainable, low-carbon operations.

I completed a PhD with an integrated MSc in Data Analytics and Society at Manchester, supported by the UKRI ESRC-funded Centre for Doctoral Training in Data Analytics and Society. My thesis on Data-Driven Modeling and Analytics for Information Propagation and Decision-making in Social Networks was a finalist for the 2026 EURO Doctoral Dissertation Award. I previously received an MEng (Research) in Mathematics from the Singapore University of Technology and Design and a BSc in System Engineering from Northwestern Polytechnical University.
